title: The End of Print: The Graphic Design of David Carson
titleBreak: The End of Print:|The Graphic Design of David Carson
lede: The 1995 monograph on David Carson by Lewis Blackwell, with an introduction by David Byrne, whose cover mixes blurred, mirrored, and substituted letters over photo fragments.
summary: Cover with a blurred, mixed-font title, a mirrored “CARSON”, and yellow, blue, and orange photo panels. Lewis Blackwell and David Carson, 1995.

source.label: Design Reviewed: The End of Print, Laurence King, 1995

made: 1995 (Design Reviewed; Chronicle Books edition, ISBN 0-8118-1199-9, per Wikipedia)

evidence.note: Inspected Design Reviewed’s scan of the Laurence King edition cover (1600 × 1600) in a scratchpad copy. The interior was not seen. Design Reviewed’s page returned 403 to scripts and was read through WebFetch. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example: the book that fixed the style’s name and reputation, with a cover title made of blurred, mirrored, and mismatched letters.

context: Design Reviewed lists the book as published by Laurence King in 1995, designed by David Carson, 245 × 285 mm. [Design Reviewed](https://designreviewed.com/artefacts/the-end-of-print-the-graphic-design-of-david-carson-laurence-king-1995/).
Wikipedia lists the US edition as Chronicle Books, 1995, ISBN 0-8118-1199-9. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Carson_(graphic_designer)).
An Internet Archive lending copy is catalogued as “The end of print: the graphic design of David Carson” by Lewis Blackwell. [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/details/endofprintgraphi0000blac).
observed: The cover is divided into pale yellow, deep blue, and orange panels, with photo fragments of a machine part and an astronomical chart labelled “Mercury” and “Venus”.
“THE END OF PRINT:” mixes letters from different serif and blackletter-like faces; several letters are blurred, doubled, or mirrored, and a thin rule runs under the line.
“DATUM” is printed upside down in a heavy sans-serif beside a vertical rule.
“THE GRAPHIC DESIGN OF DAVID CARSON” uses substituted and reversed letters: a numeral 1 for I, a reversed E, and a mirrored S in “CARSON”.
“CARSON” is very large white serif capitals over a blue photograph; the author lines are a spaced sans-serif and an italic serif.
interpretation: The cover is milder than the Ray Gun pages but carries the core traits: mixed faces within one word, damaged or mirrored letters, and type laid over photographic fragments.
borrow: Replace a few letters in a title with glyphs from other faces, or mirror them, and keep the word readable.
Blur or double one or two letters in a display line instead of the whole line.

rights.statement: No image is stored. David Carson is living, so the design is in copyright. Photographs by their sources. Scan by Design Reviewed.
